headline: Revenue accelerates, but deal costs and taxes cap earnings
summary_short: Revenue rose 34.5% y/y to $4.08 billion, powered by broad growth in the Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities segment, while diluted EPS of $1.15 trailed last year's $1.55 as one-time PA Consulting Transaction costs and higher taxes weighed on the bottom line.
summary_long: Revenue grew 34.5% y/y (+10.3% q/q) to $4.08 billion, led by I&AF's Global Operations, International and Americas sectors plus the newly-closed PA Consulting acquisition. Gross margin compressed to 19.9% from 25.0% y/y on higher pass-through-cost revenue and softer PA Consulting utilization. Diluted EPS was $1.15, down from $1.55 y/y -- a rebound from Q2 FY2026's $(0.34) loss, which absorbed PA Consulting Transaction costs -- but still hit by $50.9 million of incremental tax expense and the absence of last year's $27.4 million Amentum mark-to-market gain. Cash fell to $1.17 billion (-14.5% q/q) after funding the deal, buybacks and dividends; long-term debt eased q/q from Q2's post-financing peak. No new guidance was issued in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven primarily by the I&AF segment's Global Operations, International and Americas sectors, plus the newly-closed PA Consulting Transaction; FX translation added $21.0 million.
Compression reflects a higher share of pass-through-cost revenue and softer utilization trends in the PA Consulting business, per the release.
I&AF operating profit rose 14% on the revenue growth above, with margin impacts from pass-through cost, partly offset by higher SG&A.

Decline reflects a $10.8 million rise in PA Consulting Transaction restructuring charges, the absence of a prior-year $27.4 million Amentum mark-to-market gain, and $50.9 million of higher tax expense mostly from non-deductible transaction costs.
Tracks the net income decline above; also reflects a rebound from Q2 FY2026's $(0.34) loss, which had absorbed one-time PA Consulting Transaction costs.

Cash fell as $917.6 million was paid to repurchase remaining PA Consulting redeemable noncontrolling interests, plus $614.1 million of buybacks and $123.4 million of dividends (nine-month figures), partly offset by $1.4 billion of new borrowings.

Not narrated on a q/q basis in the release, which instead compares debt only to fiscal-year start: debt rose $1.3 billion there on 4.75%/5.375% Bond issuance to fund the PA Consulting Transaction, buybacks and dividends.
Q3 buybacks of $142.2 million and dividends of $42.5 million exceeded net earnings retained per the equity statement; the y/y decline also reflects the prior year's higher opening equity base.

MD&A frames the quarter as underlying operating performance improving (higher I&AF gross profit) while GAAP results were shaped by one-time PA Consulting Transaction costs, tax charges and the prior-year Amentum mark-to-market comparison.
